conclusions.rationale: The entry-point group, legacy flag preservation, side-effect exclusions, Windows console requirement and measurable release read budget are explicit; no new GUI surface is required.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** `handy settings` is a subcommand group of the existing `handy` executable. Existing flags (`--toggle-transcription`, `--toggle-post-process`, `--cancel`, `--start-hidden`, `--no-tray`, `--debug`, `--transcribe-file`, `--model`, `--device-index`, `--list-devices`, `--list-models`, `--repeat`, `--json`) keep their behavior; `--json` after `settings` belongs to the subcommand. It works on macOS, Windows and Linux; on Windows, output appears in the console the command was started from. A `handy settings` invocation never shows a window, a tray icon or loads a model, never triggers the single-instance "show window" behavior, and completes reads within 2 seconds on an Apple M1 Mac in a release build.

conclusions.rationale: Read, discovery, typed scalar writes, list/secret/read-only refusals, JSON flag positions and noncreating headless reads are specified with observable outcomes.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** `handy settings get [KEY]` returns all non-secret settings or one key; `handy settings keys` lists settable keys with type, allowed values or range and read-only flag; `handy settings set KEY VALUE` changes one scalar setting. Secret values (API keys) are never printed; reads report only their presence. Unknown keys return `not_found`. `set` parses VALUE with the key's descriptor type (boolean `true`/`false`, integer, enumeration value, string). Generic `set` on a list key returns `validation_failed` naming the domain command to use; on a secret or read-only key it returns `validation_failed` stating that the key is changed in the settings UI. A top-level `--json` before `settings` is accepted as equivalent to `--json` after it. A headless read never creates the settings store.

conclusions.rationale: Validation parity names both code and English reason, removes current silent fallback behavior and guarantees no mutation on rejection.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Every write goes through the same backend validation functions as the corresponding UI command, so a value the UI rejects is rejected by the CLI with the same error code and English message, and vice versa; the UI may show that message translated. UI commands that today replace an invalid value by a default (for example an unknown paste method) reject it instead. A rejected write changes nothing.

conclusions.rationale: Persisted revision, no-op semantics, expected-revision conflict details and read-modify-write under one cross-process lock give a coherent lost-update contract.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Settings carry a persisted revision number returned by every read and incremented by 1 on every committed write from any surface, including writes made by Handy itself; a write that changes nothing and a read do not increment it. Writes accept `--expected-revision N`; a mismatch returns `revision_conflict` with the current revision in `error.details.current_revision` and writes nothing. All writers (UI commands, a running instance and a headless CLI process) are serialized by one cross-process settings lock, and each writer re-reads the stored settings under that lock before applying its change, so a write without expected revision applies to the latest settings and never discards fields changed by another writer.

conclusions.rationale: Live routing, user-only transport, deadline, unknown outcome, old-instance fail-closed behavior and headless fallback are explicit and mutually consistent.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** When a Handy instance of the same user and settings store is running, the CLI sends the operation to it over a local channel accessible only to that user and waits up to 5 seconds for its answer; the instance applies it with its live state, re-registers affected shortcuts and notifies its UI. If no answer arrives in time, the CLI returns `unavailable` with `error.details.outcome` set to `unknown`, and agents must read again before retrying. If a running Handy without this channel (an older version) is detected, the CLI returns `unavailable` and never writes the store itself. When none is running, the CLI applies the operation to the settings store itself under the same lock and validation. Operations that need live state (for example the current destination) return `unavailable` without a running instance. No network listener and no MCP server are introduced.

conclusions.rationale: The foundation/output-only delivery boundary is explicit; illustrative replacement and destination stories apply after owning features land, as Clarifications states.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** This feature delivers the shared domain framework (argument parsing, file or `-` (stdin) input, `--dry-run` preview for bulk changes, atomic commit, help text per command) and the output domain for the existing output settings (paste method, clipboard handling, existing auto-submit). The domains microphones, replacements, vocabulary, shortcuts, prompts, destination and the new output settings (smart paste method, automatic Enter) are added on this framework by the features that own them (001–007, 009, 010). `handy settings --help` lists exactly the domains present in the build.

conclusions.rationale: Success/failure envelopes, details object, human mode, stderr diagnostics and export output semantics form a testable agent contract.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** With `--json`, stdout contains exactly one JSON envelope: success `{"ok": true, "revision": N, "data": …}`, failure `{"ok": false, "error": {"code": C, "message": M, "details": {…}}}` where `details` is always an object (for example `current_revision`, `outcome`, `field`, `issues` as a list of `{field, reason}`). Without `--json`, stdout shows readable text. Diagnostics, warnings and progress go to stderr in both modes. Export operations writing to `-` print only the exported content without `--json`, and put it in `data.content` of the envelope with `--json`.

conclusions.rationale: The exhaustive exit-code classes and stable code semantics support deterministic agent behavior; later domain codes are assigned but implemented by their owners.

source_citations.excerpt: **Criterion:** Error codes and exit codes are stable and documented: `usage_error` and `validation_failed`, `shortcut_conflict`, `limit_exceeded` → 2; `revision_conflict` → 3; `not_found` → 4; `unavailable` → 5; `persistence_failed` and `internal_error` → 1; success → 0. New codes may be added; existing ones never change meaning.

conclusions.rationale: The functional requirement directly preserves executable compatibility and prohibits GUI initialization; AC-001 adds measurable constraints.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Add a `settings` subcommand group to the existing executable that runs without GUI side effects and keeps existing flags unchanged.

conclusions.rationale: The generic operations and secret redaction align with AC-002 and the read story; secrets intentionally remain UI-owned.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Provide generic get, keys and set operations over non-secret settings with redaction of secrets.

conclusions.rationale: Shared validation plus locked revisioned commits aligns with the parity and concurrent writer stories and AC-003/004.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Expose one shared validation and commit service used by UI commands and CLI, with a persisted revision, optional expected-revision check and a single write lock.

conclusions.rationale: The routing requirement is refined by AC-005 to prevent competing headless writes when a running instance cannot answer.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Route CLI operations to a running instance over a user-only local channel with a 5-second timeout, or apply them headlessly when no instance runs.

conclusions.rationale: The domain framework is explicitly separated from later domain business behavior; current output is the only production domain required here.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Provide the domain command framework (file/stdin input, dry run, atomic commit, help) used by features 001–007, 009 and 010.

conclusions.rationale: Envelope and exit-code behavior is fully detailed by AC-007/008 and the error story.

source_citations.excerpt: **Requirement:** Produce the documented JSON envelope, human output, stderr diagnostics, stable error codes and exit codes.

conclusions.rationale: The success criterion sets exhaustive parity over all settable keys, an objective denominator tied to descriptor discovery.

source_citations.excerpt: Parity tests show identical accept/reject decisions and reasons between UI commands and CLI for 100% of settable keys.

conclusions.rationale: Concurrent tests must show zero lost committed fields and refusal of every stale revision, matching AC-004 invariants.

source_citations.excerpt: In concurrency tests with interleaved UI and CLI writers, zero committed fields are lost and every stale expected revision is refused.

conclusions.rationale: Every foundation-owned error must have an automated code/exit proof, with domain-owned errors explicitly assigned to later features.

source_citations.excerpt: Every error code owned by this feature (`usage_error`, `validation_failed`, `revision_conflict`, `not_found`, `unavailable`, `persistence_failed`, `internal_error`) is produced by at least one automated test with its documented exit code; domain codes (`shortcut_conflict`, `limit_exceeded`) are tested by the features that own them.
